subject: Prefix-cache billing & baseline pricing clarification
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Rate card question: are prefix-cache hits billable?

Hi Soojin,

Quick question as we map our cost model: your published rate card mentions prompt-level caching (prefix / KV cache) as a cost-saver, but its not clear whether a cache hit (where no new tokens are generated) is charged at the hosted API rate. For our workload ~70% of calls hit the prefix cache; if cache hits are still billed at the same per-token rate it changes our math a lot. Can you confirm:

- Are cache-only responses (0 new generated tokens) billed? If so, at what unit?
- If a response is partially served from cache (e.g., prefix hit + 16 new tokens), is the customer billed only for the new tokens?
- Do you differentiate billing for prefix-cache vs. full request cache (e.g., cached embedding vs cached generation)?

Were preparing a TCO comparison and also want to understand how discounts apply if we commit to volume where effective billed token volume is reduced by caching.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Priya
Priya Shah
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Analytics
priay.shah@acmeanalytics.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Rate card question: are prefix-cache hits billable?

Hi Priya — great question, thanks for the detailed callout. Short answer up front: cache-only hits do not incur generation token charges, but there are a couple of nuances Ill spell out below. If you want to discuss live, Im free today after 3pm PT.

Key points:
- Prefix/KV cache hits: when an incoming request can be fully served from the prefix cache (no new tokens generated by the model), there is no per-generated-token charge for that call. You will still see a small per-request meter entry (for routing/ingress) but its effectively negligible for billing (we treat it like a micro-unit).
- Mixed responses: if a request reuses a cached prefix (say the first N tokens) and the model generates M new tokens, we bill for the M generated tokens only. The cached prefix tokens are not double-billed.
- Cache semantics vs embeddings: embedding caches and generation prefix caches are tracked separately; embedding retrievals (if you hit cached embeddings without re-embedding) do not incur new embedding compute charges.
- Metering & invoices: youll see both the raw request counts and the billed token counts in the Console. Our billing line items show: total requests, cache-hit counts, billed generation tokens. We can provide a sample invoice extract (attached).

On discounts / committed volume: our discounts and tiered rates apply to billed token volume (the net tokens after cache deductions). In practical terms, caching reduces your effective billed volume, which reduces spend and may change the discount step you occupy. For contracting purposes we typically base a committed volume on projected billed tokens (post-cache). If youd prefer to commit on raw calls instead, we can model that but its a different commitment type and pricing.

Im attaching the current rate card and a small CSV with a mock usage breakdown showing how cache hits affect billed tokens.

Attachments: redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf (summary of hosted rates)
             prefix-cache-usage-sample.csv (mock invoice extract)

If this aligns with what you need I can loop in Marcus (pricing lead) to propose discount tiers and a mutual action plan.

— Soojin

Folks — forwarding Priyas question from Acme (high-growth telemetry customer). They do a lot of repeated prefixes (product descriptions + user state) so cache hit rate ~70% per their note. Quick ask: can Marcus propose a discounted committed tier that reflects billed tokens (post-cache), and include an optional clause where we guarantee a minimum billed token floor if they want predictability? Ideally:

- 12 month commit on billed tokens (model: projected billed tokens after caching)
- 15% discount at $X/month, sliding to 25% at $Y/month
- Optional "billed floor" at 80% of projected billed tokens to simplify their procurement math (if they miss floor, true-ups apply)

Also confirm whether were okay explicitly stating in SOW that cache-only hits are not generation-charged (legal will want the exact phrasing). Priya will want that in writing for procurement.

— Soojin
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmeanalytics.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Rate card question: are prefix-cache hits billable? (proposal + MAP)

Hi Priya — thanks for the patience. Following up with a concrete proposal that maps to your usage pattern. High-level: we will bill only for generated tokens (post-cache), and were happy to structure a committed-priced agreement that recognizes the benefit of your high cache hit rate.

Proposal (draft):
- Contract: 12 months, billed monthly.
- Commitment basis: billed generation tokens (monthly projected after cache savings). We will provide monthly usage export showing raw calls, cache hits, and billed tokens.
- Pricing tiers (billed tokens/month):
  * Tier A: up to 200M billed tokens — $0.0065 / gen-token (15% discount off list)
  * Tier B: 200M–800M billed tokens — $0.0055 / gen-token (25% discount off list)
  * Overages billed at Tier B rate + 10%
- Optional billed-floor: 80% of projected billed tokens — if actual billed tokens < floor, customer pays the difference as a true-up; if actual billed tokens exceed floor we invoice at contracted tiers.
- SOW language: explicit clause: "Cache-only responses (requests fully satisfied by prefix/KV cache with zero model-generated tokens) will not be billed for generated tokens. Billing is applied to the net generated tokens per request."

Next steps / MAP suggestion:
1) Priya confirms whether billed-floor needed (by 2026-03-26)
2) Redwood sends final SOW & rate addendum (target 2026-03-29) — DocuSign link included below
3) PoC integration and usage baseline run (2 weeks) to validate actual hit rates and finalize projected billed tokens
